caption: The two spread-spectrum techniques of pool group E8D. Direct sequence (top): each data bit is multiplied by a high-speed binary code - many chips per bit - so the transmitted signal's transitions come at the fast chip rate. A spectrum sketch shows the trade: the data alone is narrow and tall; spread, it carries the same total power over a much wider band at lower density. At the receiver the same code collapses the wanted signal back to narrow - that recovery is the process gain - while signals not using the code stay spread and are suppressed. Frequency hopping (bottom): the carrier jumps channel to channel on a grid of frequency versus time, following a pseudorandom sequence transmitter and receiver share; interference parked on one channel costs at most the hops that land on it. The pool's memory hook: the fast code shifts the carrier's PHASE in direct sequence (E8D02) and varies the carrier's FREQUENCY in hopping (E8D03) - the two definitions appear swapped as each other's distractors - and spread-spectrum receivers suppress signals not using the spreading algorithm, which is the interference resistance (E8D01).
spoken: Two panels. The top panel, direct sequence: three waveforms. The data is three slow bits - one, zero, one. The spreading code is a fast binary stream with many narrow chips inside every bit. Multiply them chip by chip and the result is a fast waveform whose transitions come at the chip rate. Beside it, a spectrum sketch: the data alone is a narrow, tall hump; the spread signal is a wide, low, dashed hump - the same total power, thinned out across a much wider band. At the receiver, multiplying by the same code collapses the wanted signal back down, the process gain, while everything without the code stays spread and is suppressed. The bottom panel, frequency hopping: a grid of eight channels against ten time slots, with a heavy trace hopping channel to channel in a pseudorandom pattern. One channel row is shaded as parked interference - only the single hop that lands there is touched. The footer carries the exam hooks: phase means direct sequence, frequency means hopping - the pool swaps them as distractors - and the receiver suppresses every signal not using the spreading algorithm, which is why spread spectrum resists interference.
